summary: IPS V5 passes the format gate but only just: recounted at 47/50 pitch words and 497/505 IPS words (spaces / hyphens split), and 41 of 46 double-spaced lines on Letter. A blank line between paragraphs spills onto a 4th page. The title page must still be copied exactly from the roster and the WInS login. V5 cannot be the base text: the team's own comment says it is AI-generated, and the 16 Oct [AI] suggestion rule does not help, because the IPS bans citations, so AI wording would be undisclosed when judged. The worst content flaw is now a rule flaw. On the team's own 16 Oct model, V5's rules pay the facility floor in full in every path and keep the gift in range in 99.4% of paths, yet leave a later operating payment short in about 6-7% of paths, with Laura keeping $0 at the 5th percentile. This reverses the case's rule that the range must protect the payments. 'High degree of certainty' is still undefined and untested, and V5 dropped the definition and since-2000 test the 30 Sep draft had. Nine plain questions about floor size, the 2031 bottom and top, the 2033 gift, 'half', post-2033 shortfalls, the leftover, waiting cash and a late 2028 deposit have no answer in V5. These rules bind after 6 Nov. Against the CFA Institute's IPS elements, V5 lacks a return objective (the payments need about 5.09% a year on $300k), allocation ranges, a stated no-rebalancing policy, liquidity, the eligible-securities constraint (the live FAQ now says the permitted list applies to 'the IPS and Final Report'), measurable review triggers and who-does-what. It names its strategy only after 165 of 497 words. On the ladder-cost conflict: $294,453 and $298,628 use the same 15 Oct curve and payments but price to payment dates versus the maturities Caplet actually holds (plus forward versus unchanged yields). The WInS bonds were sized to deliver each payment by their own maturity, so use the holdings basis for Caplet's claims, and preferably put no figure in the IPS. Several 16 Oct [AI] suggestions would add errors (a false 'only', a wrong-basis cost, 'normally $150,000', a disclosed shortfall with no owner, a range and 99% figure the brief does not ask for).

findings.title: Most elements of a professional IPS are missing: return objective, ranges, rebalancing policy, constraints, metrics, governance
